summary: Over 14 days of high-quality CGM data (98.7% coverage), this closed-loop AAPS system showed an overall time-in-range of 86% with average glucose 121.6 mg/dL, but with meaningful variability (CV 32.6%), recurrent nocturnal/early-hour hypoglycemia episodes down to 41-42 mg/dL, and recurrent afternoon hyperglycemia peaking near hour_local 16 (TAR 32.1%). No carbohydrate entries exist anywhere in the package and no declared meal-bolus strategy (prebolus, immediate bolus percentage, e-carbs) is present, so every insulin entry is a reactive Correction Bolus. This absence of carb data is the single largest factor limiting confident attribution of glucose patterns to specific basal, CR, ISF, DIA, target, or SMB/UAM settings; several plausible explanations for the same patterns (basal shortfall, unlogged meals, temporary-target-related SMB suppression, IOB stacking) remain unresolved and are not safely separable without additional data.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage 98.7%, cadence ~5 min, gap_count 10, largest gap 65 min, 0 invalid/duplicate entries; sufficient for hourly/daily pattern review. Zero carbohydrate entries and zero extended-carb entries across the entire period. A mid-period profile switch occurred on 2026-08-13 to a flat-ISF configuration consistent with the current aaps_profile; profile_context declares historical applicability as yes across the full period, treated as authoritative per user declaration though not independently confirmed by telemetry linkage.
analysis_steps.evidence: telemetry.data_quality; treatment_summary; representative_events (Profile Switch, Site/Sensor Change, GLP-1 notes, Temporary Targets, Occlusion/Pump Error); aaps_profile.created_at/updated_at; profile_context
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Zero carbohydrate logging for the entire 14-day period; uncertain performance split before vs after the 2026-08-13 profile switch

analysis_steps.findings: Overall TBR 5.1%, TAR 8.9%, CV 32.6%. Severe hypoglycemia clusters on 2026-08-13 (down to 42 mg/dL), 2026-08-14 (down to 41 mg/dL), and 2026-08-21 (42 mg/dL). Severe hyperglycemia clusters on 2026-08-15 and 2026-08-18 (285-293 mg/dL). Several therapy_response_windows show large delayed swings after small corrections, and loop statuses show basal capped by an internal safety multiplier well below the configured max_basal_u_per_hour during high-glucose episodes; peak observed IOB was about 5.94 U, far below the 25 U limit. Confounders (GLP-1 doses, pump occlusion/error, temporary targets, site/sensor changes) overlap several of these episodes in time and must limit causal attribution.
analysis_steps.evidence: glucose_extremes; daily_glucose; glucose_summary; therapy_response_windows; representative_loop_statuses; representative_events
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No exercise or illness log; cannot yet separate whether hypo/hyper clusters are basal-, correction-, SMB-, or meal-driven

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight 00:00-03:00 local shows elevated TBR (10.1-18.5%) against the lowest basal segments (0.6-0.7 U/h) and a tight 90 mg/dL target, confounded by overnight correction boluses. 04:00-08:00 local performs well (TIR 95-98.7%). Daytime hours 10-17 local show the period's worst hyperglycemia, peaking at hour 16 (TAR 32.1%) exactly where basal drops to its daily minimum (0.5 U/h); this coincides with a dense cluster of correction boluses across many separate days and, on 2026-08-18 specifically, an overlapping 135 mg/dL temporary target. Hour 19 local shows a TBR spike (15.3%) coincident with a basal step-up to 0.7 U/h. None of these coincidences are separable from unlogged meals or correction-bolus/IOB effects with current data.
analysis_steps.evidence: hourly_glucose_local; aaps_profile.basal_segments; aaps_profile.target_segments; therapy_response_windows; representative_treatments; representative_events
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate data to separate meal-driven daytime highs from basal insufficiency; no activity log for evening/overnight lows

analysis_steps.findings: Carb ratio segments cannot be validated against any logged meal since carb_entries=0 for the whole period; this sub-area remains blocked. ISF is a single flat 56 mg/dL/U segment while Dynamic ISF (70% adjustment factor) is enabled; observed variable_sens ranges widely (about 27.8 to over 120), narrowing toward a ratio near 1 during quiet periods, which is compatible with either a well-calibrated static base being correctly modulated, or a miscalibrated static base being masked by Dynamic ISF and unlogged meals; not separable. DIA of 10 hours is long; some correction-response windows show effects still evolving at 240-360 minutes, but this is equally explainable by IOB stacking from repeated close-interval SMBs (3-minute interval) rather than DIA itself.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.carb_ratio_segments; aaps_profile.isf_segments; aaps_profile.dia_hours; smb_settings.raw_settings; representative_loop_statuses; therapy_response_windows
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate entries at all; no isolated fasting/no-bolus reference window free of correction activity

analysis_steps.findings: With COB always 0 and smb_with_cob_enabled/smb_after_carbs_enabled both false, SMB/UAM operates purely on glucose deviation and is the only active automated dosing mechanism throughout the period; disabling it would remove the sole automated response given the total absence of carb logging. Delivered SMB doses (mostly 0.05-0.35 U) are consistent with the low basal schedule and configured delivery windows (3-minute interval, 15/20-minute max SMB/UAM basal minutes); no internal inconsistency found. One isolated internal multiplier outlier (UAM Boost 2 = 35.93 on 2026-08-13) did not translate into an extreme delivered dose. smb_with_temp_target_enabled=true combined with recurring 135 mg/dL temporary targets is a plausible partial contributor to the 2026-08-18 hour-16/17 hyperglycemia peak, but this does not explain similarly high hours on days without an active temporary target, so it is one of several contributing factors, not a full explanation.
analysis_steps.evidence: treatment_summary; representative_loop_statuses (cob, reason text); representative_events (Temporary Target entries); hourly_glucose_local; therapy_response_windows
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate logging to separate genuine UAM compensation for real meals from a basal/CR shortfall; no confirmation of the internal threshold AAPS uses to classify a temporary target as high

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is disabled while Dynamic ISF is enabled, avoiding a double-adjustment risk; this is internally coherent. sensitivity_ratio near 1 during quiet periods is a neutral computed adjustment, not evidence of a disabled mechanism. Wider variable_sens swings concentrate specifically around high-deviation, high-IOB hyperglycemic episodes, consistent with Dynamic ISF responding to real deviation, though a chronically miscalibrated static ISF masked by Dynamic ISF and unlogged meals cannot be excluded. max_basal_u_per_hour (12 U/h) and max_iob_units (25 U) are both far from binding in the observed data; delivered rates during severe hyperglycemia were capped near 4 U/h by an internal safety multiplier unrelated to these two reviewed settings. The carbohydrate-absorption group (min_5m_carbimpact, meal_max_absorption_hours) was never exercised since COB stayed at 0 throughout, so no evaluation is possible from current telemetry.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_settings.raw_settings; representative_loop_statuses (variable_sens, sensitivity_ratio, iob, reason text); therapy_response_windows; aaps_profile.dia_hours
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate data (blocks carb-absorption group and confounds Dynamic ISF interpretation); no independent confirmation of the high-temp-target classification threshold

analysis_steps.findings: aaps_profile.analysis_context.meal_strategies is an empty array and strategy_stable_for_period is null, meaning no prebolus, immediate-bolus-percentage, or e-carb values are declared for this period; this is a genuine absence, not an omission. All 655 insulin entries are typed Correction Bolus; no meal bolus exists in the data. Correction boluses recurrently start at already-elevated glucose (frequently 140-265 mg/dL), and several are followed by continued rises for 2-4 hours before resolving, a pattern compatible with unlogged meals handled reactively but not distinguishable from other causes without carbohydrate data.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Total absence of carbohydrate entries and of any declared meal-strategy values

analysis_steps.findings: extended_carb_entries=0 and average_extended_carb_duration_min is null; no e-carb entries exist in the period. The carbohydrate-absorption settings were never exercised (COB always 0), so no telemetry supports any assessment of e-carb amount, start offset, duration, or fit to absorption patterns.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No e-carb or regular carb entries anywhere in the package

analysis_steps.findings: Across all prior stages, the single most consistent and highest-leverage limiting factor is the total absence of carbohydrate logging, which blocks confident evaluation of CR, meal-bolus timing, and e-carb suitability, and confounds interpretation of basal, ISF, DIA, and temporary-target/SMB interactions. No profile or AAPS setting reviewed showed a clearly isolated defect independent of these confounders; automation (SMB/UAM, delivery limits, safety limits, sensitivity handling) was found internally coherent and appropriately bounded (IOB and basal deliveries stayed well under configured ceilings). The safest sequence is: establish carbohydrate logging first, then re-evaluate CR and meal-bolus timing, then reassess the two most contested basal windows (16:00 daytime and 19:00 evening) and the overnight hypoglycemia pattern separately and sequentially, changing no more than one dependent parameter at a time.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of carbohydrate logging remains the single largest limiting factor across nearly every decision area

strengths: CGM data quality is excellent across the 14-day period: 98.7% coverage, approximately 5-minute cadence, zero invalid or duplicate entries.
Early morning hours (approximately 04:00-08:00 local) show strong performance with time-in-range of 95-98.7% and low time-below-range.

SMB/UAM, delivery limits, and safety-limit configuration (max basal, max IOB) appear internally consistent, with no evidence that any configured ceiling was actually constraining safe dosing during the observed severe episodes.
Overall 14-day time-in-range of 86% with an average glucose of 121.6 mg/dL represents a reasonable baseline despite the variability noted.
issues: No carbohydrate entries exist anywhere in the 14-day period, which blocks confident evaluation of carb ratios, meal-bolus timing, and e-carb suitability.
Recurrent hypoglycemia episodes, including several down to 41-42 mg/dL, with daily time-below-range reaching as high as 12.8%.

Recurrent afternoon hyperglycemia concentrated around hour_local 13-17, peaking at 32.1% time-above-range in a single hour, with at least three unresolved competing explanations (basal, unlogged meals, temporary-target-related SMB suppression).
Isolated severe hyperglycemia clusters on 2026-08-15 and 2026-08-18 reaching 285-293 mg/dL.
Elevated glycemic variability (coefficient of variation 32.6%), which increases the risk of misattributing any single glucose pattern to one specific setting.

recommendations.title: Begin structured carbohydrate logging
recommendations.description: No carbohydrate entries exist anywhere in the 14-day package and no meal-strategy values are declared, so carb ratios, meal-bolus timing, and e-carb suitability cannot currently be evaluated with confidence. Logging real meal timing and estimated grams is a low-risk foundational step that would unblock nearly every other open question in this analysis.

recommendations.title: Defer changes to the 16:00 basal segment pending meal-linked data
recommendations.description: The 16:00 basal segment (0.5 U/h) coincides with the day's worst hyperglycemia window, but this overlaps unlogged meals, dense correction-bolus activity, and at least one temporary-target/SMB-suppression event, so the contribution of basal alone cannot be isolated yet.

recommendations.title: Monitor overnight and evening time-below-range pattern before any basal or target change
recommendations.description: Time-below-range is elevated in the 00:00-03:00 and 19:00 local windows, coinciding with basal segment transitions, but this is confounded by correction-bolus and IOB-tail effects rather than isolated basal excess.

recommendations.title: Clarify how temporary targets near 135 mg/dL interact with SMB suppression settings
recommendations.description: smb_with_temp_target_enabled is true and smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled is false; whether 135 mg/dL temporary targets are internally classified as high (suppressing SMB) is not confirmed by the package and may partially explain the 2026-08-18 hyperglycemia episode.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all current basal segments unchanged for now, given that the clearest contested windows (16:00 daytime and 19:00 evening) each have multiple unresolved competing explanations that current data cannot separate.
profile_recommendation.rationale: The 16:00 segment coincides with the worst afternoon hyperglycemia but overlaps unlogged meals and a temporary-target/SMB-suppression event; the 19:00 and overnight 00:00-03:00 windows show elevated time-below-range but overlap correction-bolus and IOB-tail activity. No isolated basal defect is supported without first removing the carbohydrate-logging gap.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Begin timestamped carbohydrate logging for one to two weeks, then reassess the 16:00 and 19:00 basal segments and the 00:00-03:00 time-below-range pattern using meal-linked glucose response before considering any basal value change.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Delivered SMB dose sizes observed (mostly 0.05-0.35 U) are consistent with the current basal schedule and these delivery limits; one isolated internal multiplier outlier did not translate into an extreme delivered dose, so no change is supported by a single occurrence.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Both limits are far from binding in the observed data: peak IOB reached approximately 5.94 U and delivered rates during severe hyperglycemia were capped near 4 U/h by an unrelated internal safety multiplier, not by these settings.

Configuration is internally coherent, with only one sensitivity-adjustment mechanism active at a time. Observed sensitivity behavior is consistent with correct dynamic response to real deviations, though a masked static ISF miscalibration cannot be fully excluded without carbohydrate data.
This group was never exercised during the observed period since carbs-on-board remained at 0 throughout; no telemetry exists to evaluate it, so any change would be unsupported speculation.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Continue relying on the current fully automated correction-based approach (SMB/UAM) as the sole active dosing mechanism, since no declared meal-strategy values (prebolus timing, immediate bolus percentage) exist and no carbohydrate entries or e-carb entries were logged anywhere in the 14-day period; introducing e-carbs or a specific bolus percentage now would require inventing meal composition that is not present in the data.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: aaps_profile.analysis_context.meal_strategies is an empty array and strategy_stable_for_period is null, and telemetry confirms zero carbohydrate entries with every insulin entry recorded as Correction Bolus; SMB/UAM is therefore necessarily the only active response mechanism, and no prebolus, immediate-bolus, or e-carb pattern can be derived without inventing missing meal data.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log carbohydrate grams and timestamps for real meals over the next one to two weeks so prebolus timing, immediate bolus percentage, and e-carb suitability can be evaluated against actual glucose response.

exceptions.pattern: Late-morning to midday corrections (approximately 09:00-14:00 local) that start at moderately elevated glucose and are followed by further rises for one to two hours before decline, recurring across at least six separate days.
exceptions.suggestion: If meals are occurring in this window, prioritize carbohydrate logging here first.
exceptions.rationale: This is the most consistent recurring under-correction-then-rise shape observed in therapy_response_windows.

exceptions.pattern: Mid-afternoon to early-evening corrections (approximately 15:00-18:00 local) followed by large glucose falls within two to four hours, recurring across at least four separate days.
exceptions.suggestion: Treat this window as a possible IOB-stacking or DIA-tail effect rather than assuming meal-related under-dosing.
exceptions.rationale: This recurring rapid-fall shape is distinct from the late-morning pattern and is more consistent with cumulative insulin action than with a meal-timing issue.

implementation_steps: Begin timestamped carbohydrate logging (grams and meal time) for one to two weeks before making any insulin-dosing parameter changes.
After carbohydrate data is available, reassess carb ratio segments and meal-bolus timing before touching any other dependent setting.
Separately reassess the 16:00 basal segment and its relationship to the afternoon hyperglycemia peak, changing only this one segment at a time if evidence supports it.
Separately reassess the 19:00 basal segment and the overnight 00:00-03:00 time-below-range pattern only after the 16:00 basal review is complete.
Revisit ISF and DIA only after basal and carb ratio findings are validated with meal-linked data, changing one setting at a time.
Clarify with the care team or AAPS documentation how temporary targets near 135 mg/dL interact with smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled before considering any automation change.
Discuss every proposed change individually with the care team, apply one change at a time, and monitor glucose closely after each change.
education: SMB and UAM operate on glucose deviation and delta, not on logged carbohydrates, when smb_with_cob_enabled and smb_after_carbs_enabled are both false; this is why zero carb entries still resulted in active automated dosing throughout the period.
A sensitivity_ratio near 1 in a loop status is a neutral computed adjustment for that moment, not evidence that Autosens or Dynamic ISF is disabled or malfunctioning.

Insulin-on-board effects visible many hours after a bolus can result either from a long Duration of Insulin Action setting or from stacking of several closely spaced automated microboluses; these two causes can look similar in glucose data and require separate verification.

A temporary target value does not automatically mean the same thing as a manually paused or reduced automation; whether a given temporary target is treated as a high temporary target depends on the app's internal threshold, which is not confirmed in this package.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only; it does not constitute medical advice and does not replace guidance from a qualified diabetes care team.
Every proposed change in this analysis must be independently verified by the user and discussed with a care team before being applied.
Change only one setting at a time and monitor glucose closely afterward, especially given the recurring severe hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia episodes identified in this period.
Do not change automated insulin delivery settings automatically or without direct user action; TuneMyBG does not modify AAPS settings.

Given the unresolved competing explanations for both hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia clusters, avoid attributing any single glucose pattern to one setting until carbohydrate logging or other targeted verification is available.
